messages:
jacob_customer: Hey, hitting a bunch of 503/504s from the hosted API /v1/generate in eu-west-1 since ~09:10 UTC. Happens for both streaming and non-streaming. sample response: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"gateway timeout","request_id":"rq_9a1b2c3d"}`. App is using SDK v0.8.2 with default retries. Any advice?
sara_support: Sorry about that — will dig in. Can you share region, model, exact request body, and a couple of failing request_ids? Also which SDK (language) and approx QPS per client?
jacob_customer: region=eu-west-1, model=redwood-7b-v1, body: `{"input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}`. Failing IDs: `rq_9a1b2c3d`, `rq_9f2e3d4f`. SDK=js-client v0.8.2, ~12 QPS from a single instance, bursts up to 40.
sara_support: Thanks. Reproducing locally now. @raj_engineer fyi — might be related to gateway queuing.
raj_engineer: I ran the same payload against hosted eu-west-1 with curl. Repro steps: ```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"summarize: long doc","max_tokens":512, "stream":false}'
```
I observed `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` then `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` intermittently. Gateway logs show: `upstream reset by peer` and high `proxy_queue_depth` for host pool `rw-eu-west-1-pool-3`.
raj_engineer: Quick probe of host metrics: GPU utilization ~85%, connection queue climbing past 120 for short periods, and the request router is applying backpressure.
maria_oncall: I'm taking oncall. Pushed a short-term mitigation: disabled canary routing to rw-eu-west-1-pool-3 and rebalanced traffic to pool-1 and pool-2. Also increased per-host conn limit from 250->350 for the next 30m.
sara_support: Jacob — we made an immediate change (rebalanced hosts and bumped per-host connection limit) which should reduce the 5xx rate. Could you confirm if you still see errors?
jacob_customer: I'm still seeing a few 504s but much fewer. Thanks. Do you have a root cause?
raj_engineer: Early hypothesis: a recent kernel-level TCP tuning change combined with a subtle memory leak in the streaming multiplexer led to periodic accept stalls on pool-3 under bursty QPS. We saw `accept()` latencies spike to 200-400ms before connection resets.
raj_engineer: Gathered traces for the failing request_id `rq_9a1b2c3d`: ```
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] gateway request rq_9a1b2c3d -> routed to host rw-eu-west-1-12
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] host accept delay 310ms
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] host responded with upstream reset
```
sara_support: For customers in the meantime: recommended client-side mitigations — set SDK retry policy to exponential backoff with max attempts=4 and jitter, and lower concurrency per instance to 10 while we stabilize. Example JS: ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({retry: {retries:4, factor:2, minTimeout:100, maxTimeout:2000}})
```
maria_oncall: Filed INC-2026-451 for the pool memory leak and kernel-tuning rollback. @eng-runtime please review the multiplexer commit from yesterday (commit id `c7a4ef3`) — suspect interaction there.
raj_engineer: Also added a temporary healthcheck: if proxy_queue_depth > 80 and accept latency > 100ms, mark host draining. This should make routing avoid overloaded hosts automatically.
sara_support: Status update for Jacob: we expect full mitigation in ~45 minutes while eng-runtime rolls back the problematic change and patches the multiplexer. We'll post again once rollback is complete.
jacob_customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Can you also open a billing-safe window? We had a few retries that spiked token usage.
sara_support: Yes — we'll review token usage on your account and issue credits if the retries were service-caused. Please DM me the customer account id and I'll attach to INC-2026-451.
deploy-bot: deploy rollback `c7a4ef3` -> `c7a4e000` scheduled to eu-west-1 (canary disabled) :rotating_light:
maria_oncall: Rollback started at 09:28 UTC, will monitor.
raj_engineer: Patch for multiplexer memory leak pushed to staging, running load tests. If green, will canary to pool-2 after rollback.
sara_support: Quick checklist we did: 1) repro with curl and capture request_ids; 2) verified gateway logs and host metrics; 3) rebalanced traffic and bumped connection limits; 4) scheduled rollback of kernel/tuning commit; 5) filed INC and attached traces + failing request_ids; 6) recommended client retry/concurrency changes to customer.
jacob_customer: Confirmed — error rate dropped from ~18% to <2% after your changes. Leaving one more check window. Thanks.
maria_oncall: Rollback completed at 09:51 UTC, observability shows accept latencies back to baseline and queue depth normalized. Marking incident as mitigated; continuing postmortem.
sara_support: Final note to customer: we'll follow up with postmortem and any billing adjustments. Feel free to re-open if you see regressions. :thumbsup:
